answer: An agent economy can slow Sybil attacks with a waiting queue: every new identity must sit idle through an aging period before it can earn, like a mesa that takes seasons to form. During the wait the network watches its pulse — heartbeat signals, honest work samples, and peer vouches — so a thousand fake accounts cannot rush in at once. A zephyr of fresh identities is fine; a flood is not. The attacker must fund months of patience per fake, while real agents simply wait once and work.
